text:
Mina: FYI I'm opening a docs PR to add an interactive snippet playground for the Optimize toolkit page (batching/caching/quant). The idea: inline runnable snippets for Python/Node/Go so readers can toggle streaming vs non-streaming, and select short/long quant profiles to see example payloads. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5101 :sparkles:
Ethan: Love the idea. Will this require any infra changes or can we embed a static CodeSandbox-style runner?
Mina: Plan A is static sandboxed runners for Node and Python using our existing snippet-runner infra (read-only, no keys). Plan B is a tiny GH Pages-hosted iframe for Go snippets that only shows output samples. I added a privacy note: no real keys, and network disabled.
Priya: We should be careful with snippets that reference quant profiles  they must match the canonical names. Did you add a sync step for the quant profiles source-of-truth?
Mina: Yes, I added a small script in the PR that pulls profiles from docs/_data/quant_profiles.json and validates the snippet YAML blocks at build time. If a snippet references a non-existent profile it will fail the docs build. I also added a docs-lint rule to catch legacy keys like `q_profile_alpha`.
Ethan: Nice. Can you paste an example of the runnable snippet markup you're using? Want to check copy-paste friendliness.
Mina: Example (Python runnable block):

```python
# runnable:optkit:python
# profile: short-seq
async for chunk in client.responses.stream(model="rwr/small", quant_profile="short-seq"):
    if chunk.delta:
        print(chunk.delta, end="")
```

Mina: And non-streaming toggle variant for copy-paste:

```python
# runnable:optkit:python
# profile: long-seq
resp = client.generate(model="rwr/small", input="Summarize product goals", quant_profile="long-seq")
print(resp.output_text)
```
Priya: That looks good. Please ensure the playground shows a short note about latency/cost differences when users toggle profiles. Also add a small accessibility note so the iframe is keyboard-navigable.
Ethan: Two engineering asks: 1) DevEx wants to sync SDK example changes with the SDK repo before we land so snippets stay compatible. 2) We should add a tiny unit test that executes the snippet parsing and validates the example output structure (not full run). I can add both to the PR.
Mina: Added a checklist in the PR description: link SDK PR that updates samples, add example-output schema test (yaml schema), and add i18n placeholders for the snippet captions (we have a few non-en locales).
Priya: For localization, can we avoid running the runnable playground for non-en builds? Keep it EN-only till translations are complete.
Mina: Done. The playground is gated by a build flag. Localized captions are pulled from /i18n/en/snippets.json for now. I left TODOs for translators.
DevExBot: Reminder: DevEx will open a follow-up sync PR to ensure the canonical snippet registry in the SDK matches docs. Tagging @dev-ex.
DocsBot: Auto-note: PR 5101 opened by Mina, reviewers: Ethan, Priya. Docs CI: snippet-validate queued.
Ethan: I'll attach a small test harness to the SDK PR to verify the streaming snippet interface matches `client.responses.stream` semantics. Also will confirm Node `for await` wording is correct.
Priya: Quick UX nit: add a one-line migration blurb on /optimize/quant/profiles.md that says "If you previously referenced legacy names (e.g., q_profile_alpha), those names are still resolved but please use the canonical profiles shown in the playground." That will reduce support noise.
ina: small correction: I think you meant Mina :)
Mina: oops yes :) Added the migration blurb and a short changelog entry under "docs". Also added a link to internal bench results for the sample latency numbers.
Ethan: Great. I'll review the runnable markup and the test harness today. If green we can merge next week after DevEx sync. Thanks for consolidating this into one PR  makes the rollout smoother.
Mina: Thanks all  ping me if you find any leftover legacy profile keys in the repo and I'll fold them into the same change. Aim to land after SDK sync.
